summary: Red Hill lookout above Antietam: a 60-ft steel tower announced in 1938, later removed; only concrete footings remained on the state parcel in 2007.

facts.design: 60-foot steel fire lookout tower, as announced in 1938
facts.status_note: Tower removed; only concrete footings remained when the DNR reviewed the parcel (2007)

events.note: Assistant State Forester announced a 60-foot steel tower for Red Hill, to be built by CCC enrollees at a cost of $2,500; a forest guard was to be posted there
State acquired the 8.5-acre parcel from John Miller under a deed dated 12 December 1939

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers gave 1,040 feet (Hagerstown Morning Herald, 22 November 1938) and 1,020 feet (Farmer's Advocate, 25 November 1938); the DNR property record gives a base elevation of 1,000 feet. The story reports all three.
The 1938 Hagerstown article spells it McClelland's; the DNR report and the lookout list spell it McClellan's. The story uses McClellan's.
The DNR parcel lies just south of Red Hill, but the report says the USGS map places the actual lookout farther south along the same ridge, so the parcel may not hold the exact site.

sources.title: Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties: A Resource Document

notes_for_editor: The 60-ft height (18.3 m) and steel design come from November 1938 announcements of a planned tower; no source records the height as built, and the DNR record gives the installation date as unknown. The only staffing reference is the planned forest guard. Removal date is not given. The DNR parcel may not be the lookout's exact spot. Name spelling differs between sources (McClelland's vs McClellan's). The brief's 18.3 m is kept as the planned height.
